title: Pilot Study for a Digital Intervention on the Use of Climate-Friendly Inhalers and Improvement of Bronchial Asthma Care (CLIMATE)
summary: The main goals of the project are to support doctors and patients in using climate-friendly inhalers, and to improve the quality of treatment for asthma patients. A new digital system named CLIMATE will be used for this purpose. A central component of the project is the switch from inhalers that use propellants (which are harmful to the climate) to Dry Powder Inhalers (DPIs), which produce fewer greenhouse gas emissions.

interventions.name: 5 practices, each with one doctor and one medical assistant (MFA), and a total of 15 patients (3 per practice), will receive the PIA CLIMATE System and Patient App for three months

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients:
(1) Patients with known bronchial asthma,
(2) 18 years or older
(3) physician-prescribed inhaler,
(4) Lung function sufficient for DPI (Dry Powder Inhaler)
(5) Sufficient German language skills
(6) Use of smart devices (tablet/mobile phone) more than times/week

Practice Staff:
(1) Physician is certified as a specialist or physician in training for general medicine, general practitioner (GP) specialized in internal medicine, or general practitioner
(2) Practice treats patients with bronchial asthma
(3) Practice has at least one Medical Assistant (MFA)
(4) Practice uses calibrated spirometry
Exclusion criteria:
Patients
(1) Emergency consultation in the practice (i.e., unscheduled or urgent visit to the practice)
(2) Severe comorbidity leading to chronic dyspnea
(3) Oxygen dependence or end-stage pulmonary disease
(4) In palliative care or resident of a nursing home
(5) Pregnancy/Lactation (or: Pregnancy/Breastfeeding)

Practice Staff
(1) Practice is specialized in pulmonology (or: Practice is specialized in respiratory medicine)
(2) Practice does not have internet access.
